key_insight: Patient query embeddings can be probed for linear “guardrail” directions that reflect urgency and sensitivity, enabling simple risk scoring from text input.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help healthcare chatbots triage higher-risk patient questions faster and more consistently by flagging cases for escalation, while keeping clinician-defined thresholds visible.
method: Defined three ordinal risk axes with oncologists: Medical Urgency, Psychological Urgency, and Topic Sensitivity.
Clustered 79,658 Czech oncology search queries with BERTopic and generated contrastive query pairs using few-shot prompting.
Used difference-in-means probes on frozen embedding spaces to recover axis directions and score new queries.
evidence_signal: On 200 evaluated queries rated by two oncologists, the probes were competitive with open-weight LLMs and showed no significant difference in quadratic-weighted kappa, with much lower latency.
watch_item: The approach still needs stronger validation on new queries and new risk axes before being relied on for real-world deployment.
paper_title: CG-Probes: Recovering Guardrail Directions from Patient Query Embeddings
